text:
maria-g: Heads-up — after the 530->535 driver bump in eu-west1 we see ~12 nodes where MIG profiles vanished and GPU UUIDs no longer match what kubelet/device-plugin expects. A bunch of inference pods are CrashLooping with allocation errors.

ops-bot: Alert: 12 nodes reporting 'no MIG devices available' (node-group: rdx-gpu-heavy-eu). See alert: <https://pager.rw/INC-1234>.

raj: Can you paste the nvidia-smi output from an affected node?

maria-g: Here's the snippet we grabbed from node gpu-28: 
```
# nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (UUID: GPU-abcde12345)
# nvidia-smi mig -lgip
No MIG devices found for GPU-0
```
Also kubelet logs show device plugin error: 
```
E0301 21:10:11.123 kubelet.go:123] failed to list devices: device UUID mismatch: expected 7e2f-... got abcde...
```

sasha: Sounds like the driver upgrade caused the GPU driver to re-enumerate MIG slices and assigned new uuids for MIG instances. We hit this pattern before when kernel/nvidia mismatch forced a re-probe.

leo: Quick diagnostics: did the upgrade include a kernel module build step? Any DKMS failures in the upgrade logs?

maria-g: DKMS logs looked clean. But on several nodes the nvidia-modprobe service restarted during the apt upgrade. We also saw messages about 'MIG capability changed, reconfiguring'.

raj: Two immediate questions: 1) Did the node GPU firmware get updated as part of the driver package? 2) Are we sure the cluster's mig-config (the saved profile config) was re-applied after driver restart?

maria-g: 1) No firmware updates. 2) It looks like our mig-config daemonset failed on some nodes due to timing — it attempted to apply profiles while the NVIDIA driver was in a transient state.

sasha: Workaround idea: run reparable commands to re-create MIG instances and restore expected UUID mappings, e.g.:
```
# on node
sudo systemctl stop kubelet
sudo pkill -f nvidia-persistenced || true
sudo nvidia-smi mig -cgi 19,19,19
# re-run our mig-config apply that maps pods to MIG UUIDs
sudo /opt/redwood/mig-config/apply --force
sudo systemctl start kubelet
```
This re-creates slices and should reproduce the same topology and uuids. But it's risky at scale.

leo: We should avoid mass remediation that changes uuids under running pods. Plan: 1) Canary 2 nodes and validate. 2) If successful, roll rest via rolling-restart that cordons and drains.

maria-g: Agreed. I've cordoned gpu-28 and gpu-33. Doing a manual drain on gpu-28 now to run the reconfig script.

ops-bot: Note: reserved capacity for Dedicated customers on these nodes — need to keep downtime minimal.

raj: Alternative: rollback driver to 530 on the affected nodes (faster, less intrusive) until we have a safe mig-config reapply flow. 530 is known-good and preserves UUIDs.

sasha: Rollback is fine for a hotfix, but I'd still run the mig re-apply in our staging cluster to harden the automation so it tolerates driver restarts. Add retries and wait-for-nvidia modules up.

maria-g: Outcome from gpu-28 (canary): after drain, ran the reapply sequence with a small pause after driver restart. MIG profiles came back and pods recovered. Logs show the device-plugin re-registered with expected UUIDs.

maria-g: Command history: 
```
# what we ran on gpu-28
sudo apt-get install --reinstall nvidia-driver-535 -y
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
sleep 10
sudo /opt/redwood/mig-config/apply --wait-for-driver --retries=5
# verify
nvidia-smi -L && nvidia-smi mig -lgi && kubectl get pods -o wide -n inference | grep gpu-28
```

leo: Good. Next steps: create a runbook for future driver bumps:
- Preflight: check mig-config daemonset health and ensure it can tolerate driver restarts.
- Upgrade in small batches (canary 2 nodes).
- Post-upgrade: verify nvidia-smi mig and device-plugin registration before scheduling workloads.
- If mismatch detected, prefer driver rollback as immediate mitigation.

raj: I'll open a ticket to add a probe into our upgrade pipeline that validates MIG topology stable post-driver-install (script that waits for nvidia modules and checks UUIDs against expected mapping).

maria-g: Filed RH-1457 for the probe and runbook updates. Also tagging customers affected so CS can reach out.

sasha: For the long-term: upstream driver packaging should expose an atomic mig-apply hook or we add a initramfs hook to ensure the mig-config applies only after kernel+driver fully ready. I'll draft a PR to our packaging repo.

leo: Thanks everyone. For now we proceed with rolling remediation group by group and keep ops-bot notifications on.

maria-g: Thanks — will update when next batch completes. :thumbsup:
